source.title: Beyond Adjacent Layers: Graph-Guided Layer Fusion for Compressing Large Language Models

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures similarity between layers within individual language models and uses it for compression. It does not test whether representations from independently trained models align more as models scale or improve.
record.gate_note: The paper reports within-model layer-pair CKA similarities, not alignment between independent models. Table 2's layer-pair counts and ratios are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"]. Compression-quality results do not measure the claim's convergence behavior.
record.test_reason: The study computes CKA between layers inside each of 13 decoder-only LLMs to guide depth compression. It never compares representations across independently trained models, modalities or seeds. No result bears on any version (V1–V7). It does not cite either original source; its similarity analysis is only topically related.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find that non-adjacent high-similarity layer pairs outnumber adjacent ones by 3.6–15.9× across 13 LLMs, including at 14B. They attribute this to Pre-LN residual-stream drift and exploit it for compression (FCM). They draw no conclusion about alignment between independently trained models.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures similarity among layers within individual language models for a compression method, rather than comparing representations across independently trained models.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the chosen similarity metric affects the resulting grouping and compression performance: cosine is used by default and CKA is selected when the cosine partition meets a calibration-only degeneracy rule. On Mistral-7B, switching from mean-pooled cosine to full-token CKA narrows, but does not reverse, the reported compression-quality deficit. These sensitivities concern within-model layer grouping, not cross-model convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: In all thirteen LLMs, non-adjacent layer pairs with CKA ≥ 0.8 outnumber adjacent pairs by 3.6–15.9×.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within decoder-only LLMs, high-CKA layer similarity is more common between non-adjacent layers than between adjacent layers.

fits_no_version.finding: The same within-model three-phase block structure recurs across six model families. In it, early and late layers form one community. The authors attribute this to Pre-LN residual-stream geometry rather than any one training pipeline (§5.1, Figure 3, Appendix M).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The within-model layer-similarity structure of Pre-LN decoder LLMs is consistent across independently developed families. This is a structural regularity, not cross-model representational alignment.

record.problems: The reported similarity result concerns layer pairs within each individual model, not cross-model alignment. It uses a fixed high-similarity threshold (CKA ≥ 0.8), and the pair counts have no reported uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3's qualitative CKA matrices are omitted because they illustrate the same within-model similarity structure quantified by the Table 2 rows. Other compression and downstream-task results do not measure convergence as defined by the claim.

untested.parts: Cross-model alignment between independently trained models and its change with scale or capability.
Vision–language alignment on paired images and captions.
Shared features or subspaces across seeds of the same architecture. The study's seeds vary only LoRA recovery, not pretraining.
Mapping or stitching between separate models.
Recurrence of features or circuits across models.
Metric and input dependence of cross-model convergence. The study's cosine-vs-CKA and calibration-source checks concern within-model layer grouping only.
Incompleteness or shared-data explanations of cross-model alignment.

record.verdict_notes: Relation 'discusses' is kept only because the paper analyses representational similarity with CKA. It does not engage the convergence claim or cite its originals; 'cites_only' would also be defensible. Table 2 numbers match the rows. The calibration-source invariance (Table 19, ARI ≥ 0.842) and the Mistral full-token-vs-mean-pooled contrast are within-model method sensitivities, not evidence for V6.

versions.untested_parts: Alignment between independently trained models, and whether it increases with model size or capability.
Cross-modal alignment between vision and language models on paired images and captions.
Shared features or subspaces across independently initialized networks of the same architecture.
Mapping or stitching representations between separate models, including linear, relative, or unpaired mappings.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across different models.
Whether cross-model convergence changes with similarity metric settings or input distributions.
Whether cross-model alignment is incomplete or explained by shared training data or objectives.
